did: An ideation sketch for the owner's essay host, with nothing landed. Teen Bird turned out to be Tin Bird, the cast's tin owlet. I gave it a rig: the cast's own drawing split into moving parts, plus wings to point with, six poses by six expressions, and seeded blinks, glances, breath and the key spin from C823. I rendered a four-scene sample essay through main's motion video twice: A as the live SVG rig, which gave the same bytes on two renders, and B as a 1,440-cell sprite sheet of the same bird. Both are on a private page with a live template sheet and the proposed schema. The prototype source is kept on the claude/host-ab branch, with no PR.

calls.title: Which medium the host is drawn in
options: A live SVG rig drawn from the cast's data
A sprite sheet baked from the same drawing
calls.why: Poses, expressions and aim combine as parameters, it stays sharp in a close-up, and it is deterministic. The sheet grows with every case multiplied together (19.6 MB for six by six) and blurs at full frame.
calls.undo: Bake the sheet with the kept sheet script and render with medium sprite.

calls.title: Where the host lands in the schema
options: A new host field on a shot beside its burn-ins
A host kind in the burn-ins' closed union
calls.why: Burn-ins already have a pure frame at each time, an alpha layer over any picture, and a preview, so the host joins that family instead of starting its own.
calls.undo: Add the field to the shot schema instead; the beats' unions carry over unchanged.

left: No code on main, by the owner's word: building waits until next week.
No voice: home's speaker can't be reached from a cloud session, so the beak follows a fixed rhythm instead of word timings.
The corner region is the owner's choice: carve one out of the body or declare the host an exception to the burn-ins' no-overlap rule.
